Subject: Pilot SLO ask + contract questions

Hi Marissa / Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team is excited to test Redwood for our clinical summarization pilot. Before we sign the SOW, procurement has two asks we need confirmed in writing:

1) Availability: Can you support 99.5% uptime for the pilot rather than the standard 99.9%? This pilot is read-heavy and we can tolerate a slightly lower uptime if it lowers cost.
2) Service credits & cap: We need removal of the hard cap on cumulative credits for the pilot period (3 months). Procurement is worried that a cap could leave our risk unmitigated.

Separately — any chance of a volume discount on Dedicated capacity for this initial commitment? We are looking at a 12-month consumption window post-pilot if the PoC goes well.

Attached: internal risk memo (procurement).

Can you confirm what flexibility you have and what approvals are required? We need final terms to route internally by Friday.

Thanks,
Danielle Park
Director, Vendor Management
Medivex

Hi Danielle — appreciate the clear asks and timeline. Quick notes:

• 99.9% is our standard for hosted + Dedicated production contracts, but for pilots we can consider a temporary SLO variance.
• Removing the cumulative credit cap is an unusual request; we'd typically limit exposure for pilots.
• We can look at a commercial concession (discount) paired with a 12-month post-pilot commit.

I'm going to surface this to our deal desk and request executive signoff for either:
A) a three-month pilot at 99.5% uptime with a reduced service-credit exposure (lower cap), plus a 10% discount if Medivex commits to 12 months afterward; OR
B) a three-month pilot at 99.5% with unlimited credits but a higher commercial offset (20% discount + higher upfront).

Evelyn — looping you for deal desk coordination and to confirm what finance/legal would need for option B if they insist on removing the cap.

Marissa
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Jonas — forwarding Danielle's request and Marissa's proposal. Short summary: Medivex wants 99.5% for a 3-month pilot and is asking to remove the cumulative service-credit cap. Sales is offering two optional trades (10% discount for 12m commit vs 20% in exchange for removing the cap).

I recommend we avoid uncapped credit exposure for a pilot. Suggested executive posture:
1) Approve temporary SLO variance to 99.5% for the 3-month pilot.
2) Replace "no cap" ask with a structured cap tied to observed incident impact: cap limited to 2x monthly committed spend for the pilot period, unless exceptional outage demonstrated.
3) Approve up to 12% commercial concession for the pilot (applied as credit toward first month of Dedicated fees) in exchange for an executed 12-month commitment to start after pilot.

Rationale: mitigates Redwood financial exposure while keeping Medivex comfortable. If we still need to be more aggressive to close this logo, we can consider option B but require indemnities and additional monitoring hooks in the SOW.

Please advise with a sign-off or alternative language; Marissa — if you can, draft a clean set of terms I can pass to legal for quick redline.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Deal Desk Operations, Redwood Inference
